VirtualDairyHerdR

Simulate biologically realistic synthetic dairy herd datasets for education, research, and precision livestock farming.

Part of the Farmaverse — an open ecosystem of R livestock simulation packages inspired by the pharmaverse.

What is VirtualDairyHerdR?

VirtualDairyHerdR generates synthetic, farm-ready dairy herd datasets that mirror the structure and biology of real precision livestock farming data — without requiring access to proprietary farm records.

It is designed for:

  • Educators teaching statistics, data wrangling, and machine learning in an agricultural context
  • Researchers who need realistic training data without farm data access agreements
  • Data scientists building and benchmarking PLF models
  • Students learning R with domain-relevant datasets

Every dataset carries synthetic_data = TRUE so it can never be mistaken for real farm records.

Installation 

# Development version from GitHub
devtools::install_github("VincentTennanty/Farmaverse/VirtualDairyHerdR")

Quick start 

library(VirtualDairyHerdR)

farm     <- simulate_farm(name = "Greenfield Farm", n_cows = 200, seed = 42)
herd     <- simulate_herd(farm = farm)
milk     <- simulate_milk(herd, seed = 42)
health   <- simulate_mastitis(milk, prevalence = 0.15, seed = 42)
fert     <- simulate_fertility(milk, seed = 42)
activity <- simulate_activity(herd, seed = 42)

# Grouped summary by breed and lactation number
education_summary(fert, by = c("breed", "lactation"))

Simulation pipeline 

simulate_farm()
    └── simulate_herd()
            ├── simulate_milk()
            │       ├── simulate_mastitis()   # binary classification dataset
            │       └── simulate_fertility()  # days open, conception rate
            └── simulate_activity()           # steps, lying/standing time

Every function accepts the output of the previous step and adds columns. Enter or exit the pipeline at any stage.

Functions

Function Input Key outputs
simulate_farm() — Farm config list
simulate_herd() farm cow_id, breed, lactation, days_in_milk
simulate_lactation() herd wood_a, wood_b, wood_c, peak_yield, predicted_yield
simulate_milk() herd milk_kg, fat_percent, protein_percent, scc
simulate_mastitis() milk temperature, rumination_minutes, mastitis
simulate_fertility() milk pregnant, days_open, conception_attempt
simulate_activity() herd activity_score, steps, lying_minutes, standing_minutes
education_summary() any Grouped summary tibble

Key features

  • Wood’s lactation curve engine with breed and parity adjustments
  • Mastitis simulation — elevated SCC, reduced yield and rumination, raised temperature; labelled dataset ready for binary ML classification
  • Fertility model — logistic conception probability driven by parity, DIM, and the production–fertility antagonism
  • Activity sensors — steps, activity score, lying/standing minutes modelled on real bolus and collar sensor output; lying + standing always sum to 1440
  • education_summary() — flexible grouped summaries by breed, lactation, DIM band, or any column in the data
  • Full reproducibility via seed arguments throughout
  • Pipeline-first design — standard tibble outputs; works with tidyverse, ggplot2, caret, tidymodels, and mlr3

Design principles

  1. Biologically grounded — parameters drawn from published dairy science literature and real sensor platform experience, not arbitrary distributions
  2. Pipeline-first — every function accepts the output of the previous step and adds columns; enter or exit at any stage
  3. Education-ready — datasets designed to support teaching statistics, data wrangling, visualisation, and machine learning
  4. Transparent — all simulation logic is open, documented, and auditable
  5. Interoperable — standard tibbles; works seamlessly with the tidyverse

Contributing

VirtualDairyHerdR is part of the broader Farmaverse ecosystem. Contributions are welcome — from parameter improvements grounded in published literature to entirely new simulation modules (lameness, ketosis, calving records).

See the Farmaverse contributing guide.

About the author

VirtualDairyHerdR was created by Vincent Tennanty, a Cork-based data scientist with a background spanning precision livestock farming and global pharmaceutical technology.

Vincent has worked as a Technical Lead in a global pharma company, where he gained deep experience in regulated data pipelines, reproducible analysis, and the kind of opinionated, interoperable tooling that the pharmaverse exemplifies. That experience is the direct inspiration for the Farmaverse — the belief that agricultural data science deserves the same rigour and open infrastructure that clinical data science has built.

On the livestock side, Vincent has hands-on experience with precision dairy technology, having worked with commercial cow sensor platforms including SmaXtec and SensHub — bolus and collar-based systems that generate the exact kind of continuous health, activity, and rumination data that VirtualDairyHerdR is designed to simulate. That real-world sensor experience shapes every parameter in the package: the activity score distributions, the rumination suppression in mastitis cases, the lying/standing time windows — all grounded in what these systems actually produce on Irish grass-based farms.
